paper.title: EvoRoute: Experience-Driven Self-Routing LLM Agent Systems
paper.central_claim: An experience-driven continuously self-refining step-level router over heterogeneous LLMs dismantles the agent performance/cost/latency trilemma and improves off-the-shelf agentic systems.

provenance.notes: Configured execution identity gpt-6.1-sol supplied by dispatch; no independently exposed model receipt/session identifier. No model probing.

signatures.object: persistent step-outcome experience base and context-conditioned model routing
signatures.information: role, subtask embedding, predicted tools, historic chosen model/cost/time/local success/final success
signatures.operation: append step records; retrieve by union of three facets; estimate model metrics; prune dominated models; sample utility
signatures.output: step-specific backbone choice and expanded experience bank
signatures.conditions: reliable terminal outcomes, relevant prior cases, enough samples per model, stable prices/capabilities
signatures.feedback: local execution success and final task success; source not specified
signatures.selection_rule: append all labeled records; Pareto prune model candidates, choose Thompson sample utility
signatures.selection_data: 50 TaskCraft bootstrap tasks plus later workflow records; benchmark update partition unclear
signatures.later_use: retrieved records determine backbones at subsequent steps/tasks
signatures.failure_boundary: noncausal task-to-step credit; test-label access; history staleness, cold start and small posterior samples

gap.author_gap: Static single-model/role assignments fail heterogeneous long multi-turn agent workloads and waste cost/time.
gap.checked_gap: Experiments support useful task-dependent routing tradeoffs, not a proved intrinsic impossibility or universal tri-optimal solution.

lineage.relation: single-turn/role routing extended to experience-conditioned step choices

gap.stakes: cost and latency of multi-tool heterogeneous agents
gap.method_response: step-level experience statistics plus Pareto/Thompson routing
gap.remaining_gap: No verifier-source/stream boundary, online freeze comparison or meaningful optimality guarantee.
unresolved: Original MasRouter/GraphRouter/PromptLLM and TaskCraft source texts absent; novelty and construction/evaluation overlap not independently checked.

expectations.applies_when: Efficiency is a central deployment claim.
expectations.reason: Actual dollars and wall-clock hours reported, with cold-start cost separately; total amortization, tool-prediction cost and repeated runtime conditions not fully audited.

expectations.applies_when: Differentiated model treatment is credited with gains.
expectations.reason: Fixed model and router baselines plus greedy/Pareto/retrieval ablations are relevant; no matched experience-stream control or freeze-online-store condition.
Execution-success and task-success labels accompany append-all records; admitting failures is legitimate if labels are trustworthy, but task-level verifier source and confidence handling are absent.
Initial-store removal harms Level1 but no frozen-store/updates-off condition isolates retained stream learning.

expectations.applies_when: A growing bank is used during evaluation.
expectations.reason: TaskCraft cold start is named, but benchmark record-update timing, label permissions, test ordering and repeated-task exclusions are not stated.

claims.text: Self-evolving routing improves accuracy and reduces cost/latency across agent systems.
claims.selection_vs_test: TaskCraft cold-start separate in name; benchmark stream persistence/label access unclear
claims.result_denominator: CK-Pro GAIA 63.19%,$85.40,38.75h vs Claude58.28%,$359.32,45.14h; ReAct average74.60%,$138.40,92.23h; five benchmark sample counts AppendixD
claims.counterevidence: Not all baseline axes dominated: HotpotQA MasRouter88.50 exceeds87.80; DDXPlus Gemini81.10 exceeds79.50. No universal optimum proof.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported useful empirical resource tradeoffs on these configurations, not guaranteed tri-optimal continual learning.

claims.text: Accumulated experience and principled selection drive improvement.
claims.baseline_control: empty cold start, semantic-only, greedy, no Pareto
claims.selection_vs_test: same benchmark ablations; retained bootstrap from TaskCraft, further stream boundary unclear
claims.result_denominator: 83.02→69.81 empty bootstrap;76.50 greedy;71.70 semantic-only;81.50 no Pareto
claims.counterevidence: No frozen-store/online-update-off contrast or repeated streams.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Initial bank and routing component usefulness; continual retained-update benefit not isolated.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported stored TaskCraft step records are reused on different benchmark tasks and initial-store ablation shows utility; subsequent autonomous continual improvement and universal trilemma elimination remain unestablished.
unresolved: Source/timing of terminal task feedback and test stream writes; independent repeated runs; matched construction budgets; neighbor-source verification.

G.reason: Specific fixed role-to-model mapping and multi-turn cost/latency bottleneck are identified; router neighbors named, but claimed intrinsic trilemma is an empirical tradeoff, not impossibility theorem, and neighboring original protocols unverified.

M.reason: Record→multifaceted retrieval→empirical Pareto pruning→Thompson utility→append is reconstructable and plausibly fits heterogeneity. Correlated final outcomes do not isolate step capability; sample starvation, time drift and metric unit scaling are unaddressed.

X.reason: Persistent tuple, union retrieval, model price pool and utility weights supplied. End-trajectory success versus immediate action update timing, empty retrieval/few-sample posteriors, bounded store maintenance and stale-label handling remain incomplete.

E.measurement.reason: Task benchmark scores, price schedule and wall-clock metrics are reported. Specific success verifier/task-label derivation and runtime protocol not disclosed; §5.2 cites Claude CK-Pro55.15 unlike58.28 Table1, so aggregate reporting is not fully internally consistent.
search_scope: Full paper, Table1–4 and Appendices A–E; no explicit per-benchmark verifier audit.

E.causality.reason: Multiple actual routing and fixed-model controls plus four component removals support package/selection effects on Level1. Initial-store-off is not online-updates-off; equal exploration/history resources of trained routers unclear.

E.holdout.reason: Separate 50-task TaskCraft bootstrap is constructive; no explicit held-out stream/update boundary or source/availability of task-success labels during evaluation. Public benchmark improvements do not certify autonomous continual improvement without oracle labels or order effects.
search_scope: §§4–5 and Appendices A–E: no test stream order, frozen-store report, label-access protocol or overlap audit.

E.statistics.reason: Dataset counts and a negative architecture result are supplied; all main and ablation tables are point estimates without seeds, CIs or significance. Bayesian uncertainty inside the routing algorithm is not experimental uncertainty; frozen A2=1.
search_scope: Full §5 Tables1–3, Appendices A–E; no across-run statistics.

E.cost.reason: Explicit price table, main monetary/runtime totals, ablation resources and $28.8/3.6h cold start are useful. No common adaptation budget against router training or full amortized total, caching/concurrency controls or uncertainty is reported.

reason: Complete pinned paper and appendices; non-weight outcome bank reused for routing is in scope. Missing author protocol/control reports are evaluated weaknesses rather than unavailable full text.
rationale: 细粒度经验路由有多框架结果及组件消融，冷启动留存库确有用；在线真值来源、测试流边界、冻结库对照和重复统计未交代，不能据此认证持续自演化或三目标最优。
